claim.markdown_says: The nine transcribed rows carry inconsistent cell counts (27, 27, 27, 27, 26, 26, 27, 27, 26) against a 28-column separator row, and the first row '| Other symbols | | 9 | x | ...' carries THREE leading cells while every other row ('| | A X | ...', '| | S | ...', ...) carries only TWO. Consequently marks land under the wrong First-Symbol column: row 'N' = '| | N | x | ... | x | |' puts its second mark in data column 24 (E) instead of 23 (N); row 'E' = '| | E | x | x | x | | x | ... | x | ...' puts its right-hand mark in column 15 (cs) instead of 16 (9); row 'A X' puts its two marks in columns 17 and 18 (A X, S) instead of 16 and 17 (9, A X); row 'P' (2nd) puts its right-hand marks in columns 17, 18, 20 (A X, S, P-1st) instead of 18, 19, 21 (S, V, P-2nd).
claim.why_it_matters: Every cell of Table 10 is a normative 'symbol X may precede symbol Y' assertion. A one-column shift silently re-attributes each assertion to a different picture symbol, so a reader (or a generated conformance test) derives permissions and prohibitions for the wrong symbols - e.g. reading 'E may precede N' where the standard says 'N may precede N'.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent measurement of both sources; every specific assertion in the claim checks out, and the real damage is slightly worse than described.

PDF side (E:/Temp/specrecon/v490/spec_p490.png, 300 dpi, 2550x3300). I did not eyeball the grid; I detected it. Vertical rules (columns whose dark-pixel count exceeds 50% of the table height) group into 28 lines at x = 272.5, 358.5, 453.5, 464.5 (the double rule), 551.5, 614, 677.5, 740.5, 816.5, 892.5, 984.5, 1065.5, 1146, 1225.5, 1306.5, 1387.5, 1467, 1547.5, 1628.5, 1690.5, 1765.5, 1828.5, 1892, 1954.5, 2019.5, 2082.5, 2145.5, 2209.5. That is a rotated-label cell (272.5-358.5), a row-symbol cell (358.5-453.5), the double rule, and then exactly 25 boundaries from 464.5 to 2209.5 = EXACTLY 24 data columns. Horizontal rules at y = 450.5, 531.5, 633, 714.5, 796.5, 878.5, 959.5, 1041.5, 1123.5, 1205 = exactly 9 rows. Sampling ink inside each of the 216 cells (dark-pixel count > 20) yields, verbatim:
  9      -> 1,2,3,4,5,8,10,12,14,16,17,18,19,21,24
  A X    -> 1,16,17
  S      -> (none)
  V      -> 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20
  P(1st) -> 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20
  P(2nd) -> 5,8,18,19,21
  1      -> 22
  N      -> 1,23
  E      -> 1,2,3,5,16
This is the claim's PDF list character for character. I also spot-checked the marks visually against the rendered page (e.g. row N's second mark sits at x~2107, inside column 23 = 2082.5-2145.5, not column 24 = 2145.5-2209.5).

Column identity: rendering p.489 (spec_p489.png) shows the same grid (28 rule groups, identical column widths, offset +69 px) with the header row reading B 0 / | , | . | + | + - | + - | CR DB | cs | cs | Z * | Z * | + - | + - | cs | cs | 9 | A X | S | V | P | P | 1 | N | E - 24 labels, exactly as the claim states, with column 4 a bare '+' and columns 5-6 '+ over -'.

Markdown side. The transcription convention is not ambiguous: page-489.md carries the SAME Table 10 and every one of its 15 rows, header included, is exactly 26 cells = 2 leading cells (rotated group label, row symbol) + 24 data cells; line 11 is the column-header row '| | | B 0 / | , | . | ... | N | E |' binding data cell k to First-Symbol column k. Against that convention, page-490.md is broken. Machine cell counts of its nine rows: 27, 27, 27, 27, 26, 26, 27, 27, 26 against a 28-cell separator - the claim's tuple exactly. The first row is '| Other symbols | | 9 | x | ...' (cells 1='Other symbols', 2='', 3='9') - THREE leading cells; every other row is '| | A X | ...' etc. - TWO. Confirmed.

Reading each body row under the established 2-leading convention gives, versus the PDF:
  A X    md 1,17,18            vs pdf 1,16,17            -> WRONG (claim's exact wording)
  P(2nd) md 5,8,17,18,20       vs pdf 5,8,18,19,21       -> WRONG (claim's exact wording)
  N      md 1,24               vs pdf 1,23               -> WRONG (claim's exact wording)
  E      md 1,2,3,5,15         vs pdf 1,2,3,5,16         -> WRONG (claim's exact wording)
  P(1st) md 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18 vs pdf 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20 -> a MARK IS SIMPLY GONE
  V      md 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20 -> correct
  1      md 22 -> correct;  S md (none) -> correct
  9      cannot be read under the convention at all (its extra leading cell pushes its 15 marks to 2,3,4,5,6,9,11,13,15,17,18,19,20,22,25 - column 25 does not exist)

Refutation attempts, all failed: (a) 'the marks are merely reflowed' - no; the mark COUNT differs in the P(1st) row (9 vs 10) and the offsets differ in SIGN between rows (+1 for A X and N, -1 for P(2nd) and E), so no single reflow or uniform shift reconciles them. (b) 'it is only markdown-table formatting' - no; in a grid table the cell ordinal IS the content, and p.489 line 11 supplies the ordinal-to-symbol binding, so a displaced 'x' states a different normative rule. (c) 'the header row alignment saves it' - no; taking the rendered markdown alignment instead (body column i under header column i, header data starting at cell 4) makes things worse, shifting V, P, 1 and the rest left by one and dropping A X's first mark into the row-label column. (d) 'the claim misquotes the markdown' - no; both quoted row strings ('| | N | x | ... | x | |' and '| | E | x | x | x | | x | ... | x | ...') match page-490.md lines 16 and 17 exactly.

Concrete normative corruption: the transcription asserts 'E may precede N' where the standard asserts 'N may precede N'; 'cs may precede E' where the standard says '9 may precede E'; 'A X / S may precede A X' where the standard says '9 / A X may precede A X'; and it silently deletes 'P may precede P'.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, and one notch worse than claimed. page-490.md's Table 10 (continued) is structurally desynchronized from the 2-leading-cell + 24-data-cell convention that page-489.md uses for the same table (whose line 11 is the authoritative column-header row: B 0 / , . + +- +- CR DB cs cs Z* Z* +- +- cs cs 9 A X S V P P 1 N E). Every element of the claim is verified: the row cell counts are 27/27/27/27/26/26/27/27/26 against a 28-cell separator; the '9' row uniquely carries three leading cells ('| Other symbols | | 9 | ...') instead of two; and rows A X, P(2nd), N and E place marks in exactly the wrong columns the claim names (A X at 17,18 instead of 16,17; P(2nd) at 17,18,20 instead of 18,19,21; N at 24 instead of 23; E at 15 instead of 16). Two facts the claim omits: (1) the P (first) row does not merely shift - it LOSES a mark outright, transcribing 9 marks (1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18) where the PDF prints 10 (1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20), deleting the normative assertion 'P may precede P'; and (2) rows S, V and 1 do transcribe correctly under the 2-leading reading, and the '9' row transcribes correctly only under a 3-leading reading - it is precisely this per-row inconsistency, not a uniform offset, that makes the table unreadable. The fix is to normalize all nine rows to 26 cells (rotated label / row symbol / 24 data) matching page-489.md, re-seat every mark from the measured PDF positions listed in the reasoning, and restore the dropped P-row mark at data column 20.
